definitions.explanation: A more formal or literary expression for free time.
Used when taking one's leave, especially in formal situations.

examples.japanese: {数|かぞ}え{上|あ}げれば{暇|いとま}がない。
examples.english: There's no end to listing them all.

examples.japanese: {忙|いそが}しくて{休|やす}む{暇|いとま}もない。
examples.english: I'm so busy I don't even have time to rest.

examples.japanese: {問題|もんだい}は{枚挙|まいきょ}に{暇|いとま}がない。
examples.english: The problems are too numerous to list.

examples.japanese: そろそろお{暇|いとま}します。
examples.english: I should take my leave now.

examples.japanese: {長居|ながい}してしまいました。お{暇|いとま}いたします。
examples.english: I've overstayed. I shall take my leave.

examples.japanese: {暇|いとま}を{告|つ}げて{帰路|きろ}についた。
examples.english: I said my farewells and headed home.

notes:
{暇|いとま} is a formal/literary reading of the kanji {暇|ひま}. It appears primarily in set expressions rather than in casual conversation.

SENSE 1 — SPARE TIME:
Used in formal expressions about having (or lacking) time:
- {暇|いとま}がない: to have no time, to be endless
- {枚挙|まいきょ}に{暇|いとま}がない: too numerous to count (set phrase)
- {休|やす}む{暇|いとま}もない: not even time to rest

SENSE 2 — LEAVE-TAKING:
A formal way of excusing oneself:
- お{暇|いとま}する: to take one's leave (polite)
- {暇|いとま}を{告|つ}げる: to bid farewell (literary)
- お{暇|いとま}いたします: I shall take my leave (very polite)

CONTRAST WITH ひま:
- {暇|ひま}: free time, not busy (everyday word)
- {暇|いとま}: spare time, leave-taking (formal/literary)

The same kanji is read differently: ひま is casual and common; いとま is elevated and restricted to set phrases.
